source: Gogleva et al. (2026) Treating the Symptom, Missing the Cause
finding: Seven LLMs found a hidden fault in synthetic regulatory systems. All fixed the system more often than they named the fault.
numbers: Medium disease, 20 organisms per agent. Opus 4.6 diagnosis 0.55 rescue 1.00. Sonnet 4.6 0.35 and 1.00. GPT-4.1 0.25 and 0.65. Qwen 3.5 0.20 and 0.90. DeepSeek V3 0.20 and 0.90. GPT-5.1 0.15 and 0.40. GPT-4o 0.075 and 0.10. Non-LLM CausalSweep diagnosis 0.10.
quote: Agents can fix systems they cannot diagnose
limits: Synthetic gene-network task, one benchmark, CIs wide at N=20 (e.g. Opus +/-0.239). Diagnosis needs both component and failure mode.
agent_relevance: A right outcome is not a right cause. The agent should score cause and outcome separately and not accept a working fix as proof.

source: Gogleva et al. (2026) Treating the Symptom, Missing the Cause
finding: The authors built a known isolability matrix by simulating every fault and every allowed experiment. Only a few organisms were truly non-diagnosable, and diagnosis was poor everywhere.
numbers: 60 organisms: 14 unambiguous, 39 resolvable ambiguity, 7 structural ambiguity (no allowed experiment separates truth from an alternative). So 53 of 60 were identifiable. Diagnosis 0.31 [0.16,0.46], 0.30 [0.23,0.37], 0.12 [0.00,0.29]. Sessions 98, 273, 49. Avg 2.3 alternatives per ambiguous organism; 24 of 39 resolvable ones have one experiment that separates truth from all alternatives.
limits: Structural class has only 7 organisms, so its CI is wide. Ambiguity is defined with a noise threshold of 0.10 on a phenotype.
agent_relevance: Direct answer to gap 4 in one domain: most of the pool-versus-final loss is selection and evidence-use error, not true non-diagnosability. A diagnosability pre-check would matter for about 12% of cases here.

source: Gogleva et al. (2026) Treating the Symptom, Missing the Cause
finding: Agents barely prefer experiments that separate the true fault from an alternative, yet nearly every session meets such an experiment by chance and still ends wrong.
numbers: 43 organisms with a resolvable alternative, 6,596 pre-commit experiments. Discriminating choices 24.1% vs 19.2% under uniform random (t=4.6, 33 of 43 organisms above chance). 91% of committed sessions ran at least one discriminating experiment; 97% of those had a single-perturbation discriminating result; median 16 further experiments afterwards; diagnosis in those sessions 0.30.
limits: Oracle audit: discriminating set uses ground truth the agent lacked. 63 interventions per organism, 11.8 on average discriminating.
agent_relevance: This is the redundant-probe rate for gap 2 on 2026 models (Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5.1): about 76% of probes do not separate live hypotheses. The agent needs a probe operator that scores the split, not free choice.

source: Gogleva et al. (2026) Treating the Symptom, Missing the Cause
finding: Models read decisive evidence well when the two causes and their predicted readouts are given. They fail at saying a result is uninformative.
numbers: Probe 1 on 69 discriminating results: six of seven models near ceiling. On 43 items where the two causes predict readouts less than noise apart, Probe 1 accuracy 0.30 to 0.53; models pick the numerically closer prediction instead of saying uninformative. Probe 2 unwarranted revision in 5 to 13 of 43. DeepSeek V3 retains a supported hypothesis in only 0.74.
limits: Replay of 43 sessions, 42 from Opus 4.6. Nearest thing to a test of 'these two causes cannot be told apart by this probe'; it is a single result, not a whole model.
agent_relevance: Closest direct evidence for gap 1: LLMs do not reliably output 'this result does not separate them'. The agent should add an explicit 'uninformative' verdict and check it against the isolability table.

source: Gogleva et al. (2026) Treating the Symptom, Missing the Cause
finding: The bottleneck is working out what each competing cause would predict, not finding the decisive result in the log.
numbers: 43 organisms, same 22-experiment record. Probe 3a (causes and predictions given) 0.88 to 1.00. 3b (predictions withheld) 0.51 to 0.74, intervals do not overlap for any model. 3c (causes also withheld) 0.37 to 0.77. Live diagnosis 0.09 to 0.58. Repeating on records written by another model gave the same median gain of 0.35.
limits: Replay of Opus-written sessions mostly. Association, not an intervention on a deployed agent.
agent_relevance: A ledger that stores, per hypothesis, the predicted outcome of each probe (an isolability row) targets this failure. This supports the ledger in gap 10 and says the state worth tracking is predictions, not just names.

source: Gogleva et al. (2026) Treating the Symptom, Missing the Cause
finding: Correct diagnosis is tied to testing the true cause in both directions (contrastive probes).
numbers: Pooled: true cause never perturbed 0.00 (108 sessions); one direction 0.04 (156); both directions 0.71 (156). Both-direction range 0.53 (GPT-5.1) to 0.84 (Opus 4.6). Five cells under 10 sessions.
limits: Correlation; agents that already suspect the cause may test it more. Authors say so.
agent_relevance: Probe design rule: always pair a probe with its opposite on the leading hypothesis before committing.

source: Gogleva et al. (2026) LUCA: a synthetic world for experimental reasoning
finding: In the companion benchmark, agents often ran the experiment that separates two causes and still did not credit the right one.
numbers: Signal-malfunction organisms: 56 LLM sessions on 8 organisms; the disambiguating experiment was run before committing in 36 cases; only 1 session got any diagnosis credit (GPT-4o, 0.5). All 24 baseline sessions scored 0. Diagnosis varies about 7x across 7 LLMs, prediction about 1.4x. Organisms with indistinguishable phenotypes are flagged (n_alt).
limits: Same group and same simulator as d01 to d06, so not independent. Abstract and sections read; per-model tables not all checked.
agent_relevance: Second view of the same failure: probe done, evidence not carried into the verdict. Do not count it as a separate replication.

source: Kriz et al. (2026) Amortizing Sequential Experimental Design in Reasoning LLMs
finding: Turning on reasoning at inference does not by itself improve information gathering. Training for information gain does, at far lower cost than inference-time BED.
numbers: Gemma-4-E4B-it base, Twenty Questions, 20-question budget, 3 evaluation repeats. Adding reasoning to BASE lowered final solve rate in all categories and raised EIG only on Countries. BED-LLM is 2376 s per game vs 38.9 s for AR-BED1 (61.1x). ASIG training 2.9x slower per step. BED-LLM is only modestly better than the reasoning BASE and worse than non-reasoning BASE on some domains.
limits: A small base model; not a frontier reasoning model. Exact solve rates only in figures; I read the text, not the plots. Gupta et al. (2025) is cited there for LLMs being insensitive to feedback.
agent_relevance: Weak answer to gap 8: native reasoning in a small model did not close the information-gathering gap. Frontier 2026 reasoning models with BED-LLM were not found tested.

source: Kriz et al. (2026) Amortizing Sequential Experimental Design in Reasoning LLMs
finding: Transfer to simulated clinical questioning: five questions, GPT-5 as patient and decider.
numbers: MediQ-style, 50-disease sets. Dermatology (n=95 held-out diagnoses) accuracy 90.5 +/-3.0 to 94.7 +/-2.3; Brier 0.165 to 0.120. Other specialties (n=92) 84.8 +/-3.8 to 90.2 +/-3.1; Brier 0.227 to 0.157. Correct-answer likelihood 76.0 to 79.2 and 72.8 to 78.1.
limits: One fine-tuned model, one patient simulator, SEM over cases; a fixed GPT-5 decider carries much of the accuracy.
agent_relevance: Information-gain training transfers, but needs weight training. Our scaffold has no training, so this only shows the target skill exists.

source: Hartmann et al. (2026) Amortising Bayesian Experimental Design for Sequential Information Gathering in LLMs
finding: ASIG fine-tuning raised 20 Questions success on a 7B model but the gain mostly vanished on 14B, and BED-LLM was not robust.
numbers: Qwen2.5-7B Animals 7.6 +/-1.8 to 21.0 +/-4.8 (BED-LLM 19.2); Plants 6.8 to 16.6 (BED-LLM 22.8). Qwen2.5-14B Animals 35.0 to 39.2 (BED-LLM 26.4); Plants 11.8 to 13.6 (BED-LLM 21.0). BED-LLM 25x to 36x slower. MediQ: 7B accuracy 46.7 to 47.6, overconfidence 36.1 to 33.4; 14B 54.1 to 54.2, overconfidence 20.7 to 22.2.
limits: ICML workshop paper. Proposer models are Qwen2.5 (non-reasoning). Authors list reasoning models as future work.
agent_relevance: Gains from information-gain methods shrink as the base model gets stronger (14B). That is a warning for gap 8: frontier models may gain less.

source: Choudhury et al. (2026) BED-LLM: Intelligent information gathering with LLMs and Bayesian experimental design (ICLR, v3)
finding: Ablations separate hypothesis state from the information-gain step. A filtered hypothesis set with a simple even-split rule already gets most of the gain.
numbers: 20 Questions success %, Qwen2.5-72B, Animals: Prompt-Only 45, CoT 51, ICL Beliefs (no filtering) 46, Implicit Maximization (filtered set, LLM judges best question) 61, Split 87, Entropy 85, BED-LLM 95. Celebrities: 32, 48, 26, 39, 56, 59, 84. GPT-4o Animals: 45, 62, 25, 70, 83, 88, 93. About 100 games per cell (+/-2 to 5).
limits: All questioners are non-reasoning models (GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Llama, Mistral, Qwen2.5). Closed candidate set with a simulated answerer. The paper tests no ledger-only arm without any split or EIG scoring.
agent_relevance: Answer to gap 10: state tracking (filtered set) alone is not enough (Implicit Max 61 vs Split 87). The scored split step carries most of the gain; full EIG adds about 8 points over Split. Build the ledger and the split score together.

finding: No frontier reasoning model was used as the questioner; o3 only helped build the animals list. Free chain-of-thought gave a small gain.
numbers: CoT over Prompt-Only: Qwen2.5-72B Animals 45 to 51; GPT-4o 45 to 62; Llama-3.1-8B 8 to 19. BED-LLM stays above CoT everywhere. Runtime Table 3 shows BED-LLM costs more per game.
limits: Read from the paper text and Table 1. Absence of reasoning models is from the model list; I did not see an appendix with them.
agent_relevance: Gap 8 stays open. Do not claim the BED-LLM gain holds for o3-class or 2026 reasoning models.

source: Cloud-OpsBench (2026) A reproducible benchmark for agentic root cause analysis in cloud systems
finding: The benchmark rewards a committed root cause, with no abstain option found. Hard performance faults are where telemetry cannot separate causes.
numbers: JRA by difficulty: OnlineBoutique GLM-5.1 0.91/0.73/0.58, DeepSeek-V4-Flash 0.92/0.72/0.57, Qwen3.5-27B 0.87/0.71/0.41. TrainTicket GPT-5 0.88/0.89/0.00, GLM-5.1 0.73/0.56/0.00, Qwen3.5-Plus Hard 0.29, DeepSeek-V4-Flash 0.22. Audit of right-answer-poor-process cases: 95% from incomplete investigation; 73% stopped at a symptom log; 22% 'inconclusive evidence and heuristic guessing' where observations stayed ambiguous.
limits: I searched the text for abstain, inconclusive, ambiguous: no abstention option or score appears. Hard faults mix a true telemetry limit with missing source access (see K20).
agent_relevance: Answer to gap 6 for this benchmark: guessing is rewarded and 'need another probe' has no credit. A 22% share of audited cases ended ambiguous, so an abstain-or-probe rule has room to help but nobody measured it.

finding: Repeated-call and evidence-completeness numbers give a proxy redundant-probe rate for 2026 models.
numbers: OnlineBoutique: Qwen3-8B 15.78 steps, EE 0.34, ECR 0.19, RAR 0.45 (45% of calls repeat an earlier tool-argument pair). Qwen3-14B 14.18 steps, EE 0.32, RAR 0.26, ECR 0.55. GPT-5 5.56 steps, EE 0.64, RAR near 0, ECR 0.39. GLM-5.1 7.75 steps, EE 0.54, ECR 0.65. TrainTicket RAR 0.22 and 0.31 for the two Qwen models. Authors propose planners that use unresolved alternatives and expected information gain as future work.
limits: RAR counts exact repeats only; a non-repeated probe can still split nothing. Not an EIG=0 rate.
agent_relevance: Strong models stop early (GPT-5) while weak ones repeat. Both fail differently. The agent needs a stop rule tied to unresolved alternatives, not step count.

source: Jaradat et al. (2026) An LLM-orchestrated neuro-symbolic framework for verifying diagnostic signal reachability in electronic systems
finding: Nearest hardware-diagnosability study: it decides whether a fault signal can be observed at all. A graph search makes the verdict, and the LLM only labels device roles.
numbers: Five production boards, 421 expert-graded signals (52 negatives). Pooled F1 0.578 (S1) to 0.944 (S3). Precision and specificity 100% at every stage (95% upper bound on false-positive rate 5.8%, rule of three). Motherboard recall S1 to S3 27.9 to 95.9; accelerator 59.7 to 84.0; HDD 8.3 to 55.9; SCM 48.5 to 66.7 (PCIe row garbled in text extraction, not quoted). 91 signals flagged as unmonitored.
limits: This is observability, not isolability between two faults. The paper says LLMs are unreliable at structural connectivity but reports no LLM-only arm. Only 52 negatives.
agent_relevance: Supports the design choice that the separability verdict should come from code over the model, not from LLM judgement. It does not test whether an LLM can decide diagnosability, so gap 1 stays open.

finding: Swapping the LLM kept precision at 100% while recall moved with the model's device understanding.
numbers: SCM module, three LLMs, five clean-slate runs each. Mean accuracy 88.52 +/-1.17, 88.08 +/-2.85, 80.43 +/-8.16. Runtime about 3 to 21 minutes. Precision exactly 100% for all three.
limits: One module, anonymous model labels (A, B, C), small negative set.
agent_relevance: When a check is done by a deterministic procedure, LLM choice affects coverage but not soundness. Use the same split for the isolability check.

source: DistDebug-Bench (2026) Can LLM agents diagnose bugs in distributed systems?
finding: Benchmark of real distributed-system bugs. Authors name two failure modes: tunnel vision from no explicit reasoning structure, and nondeterminism from inconsistent tool scope.
numbers: 120 real bugs, 11 systems, 5 languages, 10 failure patterns. Scores not read (abstract page only).
limits: Abstract only. No numbers on tunnel vision rate or ambiguity.
agent_relevance: Tunnel vision is the same failure as the stuck leading hypothesis; a ledger with a forced split probe is the scaffold counter. Needs the full paper before use.

source: Sequential Bayesian optimisation with five frontier LLMs (arXiv 2609.33061, 2026)
finding: Frontier LLMs overreact to new data, act exploitatively while stating intent to explore, and removing in-context history restores exploration.
numbers: Five LLMs, seven combinatorial chemistry and biology datasets. No configuration clearly beat a mean statistical baseline. Per-model numbers not read (abstract only).
limits: Abstract only; Bayesian optimisation, not diagnosis.
agent_relevance: Backs the idea that holding belief in context ('context-stickiness') hurts and that an external ledger should carry state (gap 10), but numbers are not in hand.

source: Adaptive group elicitation via multi-turn LLM interactions (arXiv 2602.14279, 2026)
finding: An independent group scored candidate questions by LLM-estimated expected information gain and got gains in survey-opinion prediction.
numbers: Three real opinion datasets; on CES with 10% respondent budget, relative gain over 12%. Cost and token matching not checked.
limits: Abstract only. Different task (population surveys), not diagnosis, and not compared at equal tokens to best-of-N.
agent_relevance: A different-group use of the EIG idea (partial support for gap 3), but SIA itself has still not been replicated.
